sentenceFrames: Attribution + Definition: According to the article, a government shutdown happens when U.S. Congress cannot agree on a new federal budget before a deadline.

Cause & Permission: Because lawmakers in the House of Representatives and the Senate disagree on spending, programs, taxes, or debt limits, the government has no permission to spend money, so many services must pause.

Stays Open vs. Gets Paused: During a shutdown, military and national security, air traffic control, mail delivery, and mandatory Social Security and Medicare payments stay open, while national parks, museums, NASA, science labs, and safety inspections may close or pause.
Workers & Conclusion: Overall, a shutdown creates hardship for families because some workers still have to work without immediate pay while many others are furloughed, or sent home without pay.
paragraphOutline: 1. Topic & Definition (with Attribution): Begin with "According to the article," and define a government shutdown (Congress failing to agree on a federal budget before a deadline).
2. Cause & Permission: Explain that Congress (House of Representatives and Senate) must vote, what lawmakers disagree on, and why missing the deadline removes permission to spend money.
3. Services Comparison: Contrast services that stay open (including mandatory programs) with services that may close or pause.
4. Workers & Families: Explain both worker impacts (working without immediate pay vs. being furloughed without pay).
5. Conclusion: Close with "Overall," or "In conclusion," summarizing the dual impact on services and families.

commonMistakes.mistake: A government shutdown happens because Congress doesn’t want to pay for parks and closes everything.
commonMistakes.correction: According to the article, a government shutdown happens when Congress cannot agree on a new federal budget before a deadline, so the government loses permission to spend money and many services—not all—must pause.
commonMistakes.explanation: Two errors: misses the budget deadline/permission mechanism and falsely claims everything closes (Section 4 explicitly lists services that stay open).

commonMistakes.mistake: During a shutdown, many workers furlough home and Social Security stops.
commonMistakes.correction: During a shutdown, many government workers are sent home without pay (called being "furloughed"), while Social Security and Medicare payments stay open because they are mandatory programs.
commonMistakes.explanation: Grammar and fact error: "furloughed" requires passive voice ("are furloughed" / "are sent home"), and Social Security stays open.

commonMistakes.mistake: National parks always close and military workers get paid right away.
commonMistakes.correction: National parks and museums may close, while military and national security stay open, although workers may not be paid right away.
commonMistakes.explanation: Modal/fact precision error: the article uses "may close" (possibility) and warns that military workers "may not be paid right away."

commonMistakes.mistake: Democrats (or Republicans) always cause shutdowns every October 1.
commonMistakes.correction: According to the article, if lawmakers (usually Democrats and Republican lawmakers) disagree on spending, programs, taxes, or debt limits and no agreement is reached by the deadline, shutdown happens.
commonMistakes.explanation: Outside fact & neutrality violation: do not blame one party or insert outside dates/claims not present in the article.

teacherCorrectionFocus: Verify source attribution ("According to the article,") and 100–140 word range.
Check passive voice ("is made up of", "is reached", "are sent home", "are furloughed") and modals ("may close", "must pause").
Confirm both sides of Section 4: open vs. paused services AND delayed-pay workers vs. furloughed workers.
Remove any partisan blame or outside facts not written in the canonical source.
finalWritingSupport.g1Scaffold: Give G1 students the 5-step Paragraph Outline and let them adapt one sentence frame per step, focusing on "when/because/so", "while/however", and accurate key terms (federal budget, deadline, permission, mandatory, furloughed).
finalWritingSupport.g2Extension: Challenge G2 students to integrate at least two passive forms, one parallel list, and precise modal hedging ("may close", "may not be paid right away") within 115–130 words.
